newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Bank of Taiwan cuts prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Taiwan cuts prime lending rate.

text.p: Bank of Taiwan, Taiwan's largest state-run bank, said on Wednesday it was cutting its prime lending rate by 0.025 percentage points to 7.050 percent from 7.075, effective on Wednesday.

"To reflect the current loose liquidity in the market and to cope with the government's economy-boosting policy, Bank of Taiwan decides to lower prime lending rate and other rates," the bank said in a statement.
The bank was also cutting its one-month to three-year time deposits rates by between 0.10 and 0.25 percentage points, also effective from Wednesday, the statement said.
The bank last cut its prime lending rate on August 28 by 0.025 percentage points to 7.075 percent from 7.100, it said.
The move followed the rate cuts by the Big Three state-run banks -- Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank and Hua Nan Bank, which cut their prime lending rates and time deposits rates in early October.
